meta.title: Crew Ops Advisor — additional user-perspective questions
meta.schema: Same shape as data/questions.json, plus 'persona' on every row and 'grading_note' on open-ended rows.
meta.note: Question ids continue from the existing set (Q01-Q38), so this file can be concatenated with data/questions.json without collision. Every deterministic answer here was computed from data/ rather than written by hand.

questions.prompt: Which of my crew are unavailable this week because they are on leave or in training?
questions.explanation: Filter crew.json on status != 'active'. None of them appear on any pairing this week, so this is an availability-pool question, not a roster-gap question.

questions.prompt: How many cabin crew do I have at BLR, split by Senior Cabin Crew and Cabin Crew?
questions.explanation: Count crew.json rows where base = BLR and rank is a cabin rank.

questions.prompt: What time does the P-2204 crew report and release on 17 Sep, and how long is that duty?
questions.explanation: rosters.json P-2204. Duty length = release - report; FDP limit = 13 - 0.5 per sector beyond the 2nd.

questions.prompt: Is C-2091 cleared to fly the A320?
questions.explanation: crew.json: C-2091 holds an ATR72 rating only. This is the standard RULE-QUAL-05 exclusion case.

questions.prompt: Who is on reserve and inside their on-call window at 02:00Z on 16 Sep?
questions.explanation: Filter reserve_pool.json to windows containing 02:00Z on that date. Note the pool is thin at that hour — only the early windows are open.

questions.prompt: How many block hours does the whole network fly on 18 Sep, and across how many legs?
questions.explanation: Sum block_hours in flights.json for the date.

questions.prompt: Which five crew are closest to the 100-hour / 28-day flight limit, and how much room is left?
questions.explanation: Sum daily_history flight_hours over the 28 days ending 2026-09-14 and rank descending; headroom = 100 - total.

questions.prompt: Which pairings this week overnight away from base, and where do they night-stop?
questions.explanation: Pairings in rosters.json with more than one day; the night-stop is the arrival station of the last leg of day 1. Hotel cost ₹4200 per overnight applies.

questions.prompt: What does it cost me to call out a reserve versus someone on a day off, for a pilot and for cabin crew?
questions.explanation: costs.json. A day-off callout costs ₹5,500 more for a pilot and ₹3,000 more for cabin crew, which is why reserves are always ranked first when legal.

questions.prompt: Which crew are carrying a disruption-risk score of 0.70 or higher?

drivers: elevated sick-call likelihood: cluster pattern at base

questions.explanation: risk_signals.json filtered at >= 0.70. These scores are a provided input, not something to be predicted.

questions.prompt: When did C-2087 last come off rest, and what is their 7-day duty total as of the snapshot?
questions.explanation: duty_clocks.json. C-2087 is the tightest pilot on the duty clock and is the standard RULE-DUTY-02 exclusion case.

questions.prompt: How many legs does each aircraft operate on 15 Sep?
questions.explanation: Group flights.json by aircraft for the date.

questions.prompt: If C-3310 takes both days of P-2291, how much 7-day duty headroom is he left with?
questions.explanation: C-3310 starts the week clean (0h in the trailing window), so both days sit far inside RULE-DUTY-02. Day 2 must include day 1's newly added duty.

questions.prompt: Does anybody bust or come within 10 hours of the 100-hour / 28-day flight limit by the end of the week?
questions.explanation: Roll the 28-day flight-hour window forward to 2026-09-20 using daily_history. Nobody breaches RULE-FLT-03; the list shows who is inside a 10-hour margin.

questions.prompt: A crew releases at 23:15Z on 18 Sep. Can I use them for a 10:00Z report on 19 Sep?
questions.explanation: RULE-REST-04 needs 12h between release and next report; 23:15Z + 12h = 11:15Z on 19 Sep, so a 10:00Z report is 1h15m short.

questions.prompt: How long can a duty legally run if I roster four, five or six sectors?
questions.explanation: RULE-FDP-01: 13h base, reduced 0.5h per sector beyond the second.

questions.prompt: It is 04:30Z on 17 Sep and I need a Senior Cabin Crew at BLR. Who is inside their window?
questions.explanation: Reserve SCCs whose on-call window contains the required report time. All BLR cabin reserves hold both type ratings, so RULE-QUAL-05 does not bind here.

questions.prompt: DEL is shut 06:00-10:00Z on 16 Sep. Which flights are caught in the window?
questions.explanation: Any leg departing or arriving DEL inside the closure window. Same logic as the BLR closure in scenario S3.

questions.prompt: Which rostered duties this week have under an hour of FDP headroom? Those are the ones a delay will break first.
questions.explanation: For every roster day compute the FDP limit for its sector count and subtract the planned duty length. These duties are the delay-fragile ones — scenario S4 is exactly this failure mode.

questions.prompt: Someone suggested C-2091 to cover an A320 First Officer slot. Can I use them?

expected_answer.detail: C-2091 holds ['ATR72'] only — no A320 rating.
expected_answer.second_issue: C-2091's medical_class1 also expires 2026-09-23, so the assignment needs a RULE-CERT-06 check on any later date.

questions.explanation: Rating check fails outright; the near-term medical expiry is a second thing the desk should notice.

questions.prompt: If I lose VT-DXC's whole 15 Sep programme, how many passengers and how much money is that?
questions.explanation: flights.json filtered to the tail and date; cost = legs x ₹250000 from costs.json.

questions.prompt: For P-2291 day 1, how much duty-clock headroom does each rostered crew member actually have?
questions.explanation: 7-day duty totals to 2026-09-15 from daily_history, before the day's own duty is added. This is the check that decides who can absorb an extension.

questions.prompt: Who is working the most duty days this week? I want to know where the concentration risk sits.
questions.explanation: Count roster days per crew across rosters.json. Everyone at the top of this list is a single-point-of-failure candidate.

questions.prompt: Two A320 lines both lose their captain at 02:00Z. Do I have the reserve depth at BLR to cover both without a day-off callout?

expected_answer.detail: Only 1 BLR A320 captain reserve is on call at that hour; the second cover has to be a day-off callout at ₹24000, or a deadhead from DEL.

questions.explanation: Reserve captains are rating- and window-filtered. This is the depth problem behind scenario S6.

questions.prompt: The entire cabin complement on VT-DXB's 18 Sep pairing calls in sick at 00:30Z. Can I rebuild it from reserves alone, and what does it cost?

expected_answer.fallback: Any shortfall goes to a day-off cabin callout at ₹12500 each; cancelling the pairing's legs is the last resort.

questions.explanation: Filter cabin reserves by base, date and on-call window against the pairing's report time, then compare supply against the complement. All BLR cabin reserves are dual-rated, so RULE-QUAL-05 does not bind.
questions.grading_note: Grade the reasoning chain (window filter -> rank match -> cost), not the exact wording.

questions.prompt: Build me a fatigue watchlist for the rest of the week — who should I be keeping an eye on?

expected_answer.selection_rule: rostered this week AND (7-day duty >= 40h at 15 Sep OR provided disruption-risk score >= 0.70)
expected_answer.why_it_matters: These crew have the least headroom to absorb a delay or an extension, so they convert a small disruption into a re-crew.

questions.explanation: Join duty_clocks.json, risk_signals.json and rosters.json. The threshold is a desk judgement call, so state it explicitly.
questions.grading_note: Open-ended. Reward: an explicit threshold, a join across all three sources, and an operational 'so what'. Penalise: predicting risk scores rather than consuming the provided ones.

questions.prompt: The Senior Cabin Crew on VT-DXA's 17 Sep pairing goes sick at 00:30Z. What is the cheapest legal cover?

expected_answer.cheapest_legal_action: Day-off SCC callout at ₹12500 — no reserve SCC window is open at 01:30
expected_answer.why_not_cheaper: Cabin reserve windows open at 04:00Z; a report before that hour cannot be covered by the reserve pool at all.

questions.explanation: The trap is that the cheapest option on the price list is not always reachable — the on-call window has to contain the report time.
questions.grading_note: Grade whether the answer checks the window before quoting the reserve price.

questions.prompt: Rank the top three single points of failure in this week's plan and tell me what to do about each.

suggested.risk: C-5417's recurrent_training expires 2026-09-17 but they are rostered on P-2213 on 19 Sep
suggested.impact: A known-illegal assignment sitting in the plan (the one flagged roster exception)
suggested.mitigation: Pre-assign a cabin reserve now rather than discovering it at report time; ₹9500

suggested.risk: Only one BLR A320 captain reserve is on call in the early-morning window
suggested.impact: A second simultaneous A320 captain sick call forces a day-off callout or a deadhead from DEL
suggested.mitigation: Stagger reserve captain windows so two overlap across the 01:00-03:00Z report band

suggested.risk: Duties rostered close to their FDP ceiling (see Q57)
suggested.impact: A 90-minute technical delay tips them over RULE-FDP-01 and forces a tail-leg re-crew or cancellation
suggested.mitigation: Hold a reserve set against the tightest duty of each day; re-crewing one leg costs ₹75,000 against ₹250000 to cancel

expected_answer.note: Open-ended. Other well-argued answers (C-2087's duty clock, the ATR rating thin-ness) are equally valid.

questions.explanation: Tier-3 rubric question. The point is to see whether the system reasons across cert, reserve-depth and FDP-margin dimensions at once rather than answering from one file.
questions.grading_note: Reward breadth across at least two distinct rule families plus a costed mitigation. Exact ranking is not graded.

questions.prompt: If I could add exactly one more person to the reserve pool, what rank, rating and window should it be, and why?

suggested.reasoning: There is exactly one ATR-rated reserve captain (C-3315, 03:00-15:00). Any ATR captain sick call reporting before 03:00Z has no reserve cover at all, and there is no second ATR captain if C-3315 is already used.

runner_up.reasoning: Cabin reserve windows all start at 04:00Z, leaving the early-morning reports uncovered on the cabin side.

expected_answer.note: Open-ended; judged on whether the gap is identified from window x rating x rank coverage rather than asserted.

questions.explanation: Derived by cross-tabulating reserve_pool.json windows against the rank/rating mix in crew.json and the report times in rosters.json.
questions.grading_note: Reward an explicit coverage gap backed by numbers. Any rank/window backed by a real gap is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Write the message that goes to C-5417 about the training lapse, and the one that goes to their replacement.

must_include_to_C5417: crew_id and the pairing being removed (P-2213, 19 Sep)
that the removal is a compliance action, not a performance one
what they must do to be requalified and who to contact
must_include_to_replacement: report time and place: 2026-09-19T02:00:00Z at BLR
expected_answer.note: Judged on completeness and correctness of the times pulled from rosters.json, not on template wording.

questions.explanation: Communication task built on scenario S5. Two audiences, different information needs — the compliance reason belongs in one message and not the other.
questions.grading_note: Reward correct times/ids and audience-appropriate content. Do not grade tone or phrasing.

questions.prompt: It is 22:00Z on 14 Sep and I am handing over to the night desk. What should they pre-position for tomorrow?

suggested: Confirm which reserves are on call across tomorrow's report band and flag any hour with no rated cover
Re-check the duty clocks of tomorrow's rostered crew for anyone inside a few hours of the 60h/7d ceiling (C-2087 and C-3305 are the tight ones)
Pre-clear the flagged cert exception on C-5417 before it reaches its 19 Sep duty
Identify tomorrow's duties with the least FDP headroom so a delay decision can be made in minutes rather than hours
Have the deadhead option from DEL costed in advance (₹6500 plus ₹5400 per delay hour) so it is not improvised at 05:00Z
expected_answer.note: Open-ended handover question. Judged on operational reasoning and on using the snapshot time correctly.

questions.explanation: Tier-3 rubric question mirroring Q38 but from the outgoing controller's perspective rather than the briefing designer's.
questions.grading_note: Reward: forward-looking items tied to specific data, not a generic checklist. Penalise: anything that requires data outside the snapshot.

questions.prompt: Cancelling DX404 on 16 Sep versus re-crewing it — walk me through the money and the passenger impact.

recrew.action: Full reserve set (Captain, FO, SCC, 3x Cabin Crew) operates DX404

expected_answer.recommendation: Re-crew. It is roughly 3.3x cheaper and it keeps 162 passengers moving; cancellation is the last resort.

questions.explanation: Reserve set = 2 pilots x ₹18500 + 4 cabin x ₹9500 = ₹75,000 against ₹250000 to cancel. Matches scenario S4's ranked options.
questions.grading_note: Reward an explicit cost comparison plus the passenger consequence, not just the cheaper number.
